correctness.rationale: The common monic quadratic \(z^2+z=S\) forces at most two coordinate values. For each nonempty proper coordinate subset, all solutions correspond exactly to roots of \((n-1)a^2+(2(n-r)-1)a+(n-r)=0\). The proof counts constants, adjusts for coincident roots when \(p\mid(n+1)\), applies the discriminant \(1-4r(n-r)\) in odd nonsingular characteristic, and in the singular case solves a linear equation. In characteristic two it uses \(\operatorname{Tr}(1)\equiv m\pmod2\). Every case covers all \(n\ge3\) and finite fields. Direct multiplication brute force agreed in eighteen small test cases.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The survey bounds the scheme length by \(2^n\) for a perfect evolution algebra and averages the nonzero idempotent number over all invertible structure matrices; neither implies rational counts of the specific \(J-I\) matrix. Moreover \(p\mid n-1\) makes \(J-I\) singular, excluding that branch from perfect-algebra bounds. The complex regular-algebra existence theorem in the 2025 note is a weaker statement in a different coefficient-field scope.

value.rationale: All idempotent elements are classified and counted for the natural unweighted complete graph in every dimension and every finite field. This includes the singular/nonperfect case where generic perfect-algebra bounds do not apply and a sharp extension-degree-parity transition within characteristic two. These fixed points encode equilibria of the quadratic evolution operator and are motivated by field-dependence questions, rather than by an arbitrary numerical slice.
